about: What jetcarp-field-test.sh and jetcarp-field-test.ps1 run, tier by tier. Each test names its tiers, the command line it runs (every one a subcommand: never the app, never the background host, nothing drawn on screen), how its result is read (its kind, which both scripts know), its time on a typical laptop, and the oldest release with what it needs (`from`, and `to` where it stops applying). A release outside a test's range skips it, saying why. README.md says how to change this file.

tiers.name: Quick
tiers.about: what JETCARP sees on this computer, its JETCARP Hardware Score, and a first check that the GPU and the processor agree

tiers.name: Suite
tiers.about: Quick, plus all 371 scenes on the processor and each GPU, two soup hunts with known results, Fit to this computer off screen, HashLife, and stepping speed

tiers.name: Extended
tiers.about: Suite, plus 40 scenes run for 5,000 generations, the scenes again through every other graphics API, and a 15-minute search with its memory watched

parity.about: The scenes and the hashes every machine must reach, from the release-candidate test records (each cycle's parity set: README.md). A set is used for the releases from `from` to `to`, and `to` is the newest release the set was checked with: a later release isn't checked yet, so it runs the scenes anyway and compares the processor with each GPU, until its candidate has been checked and `to` moved on (README.md).

tests.name: What JETCARP sees here
tests.about: the system, processor, memory, graphics adapters and drivers, and the GPU self-test, as `jetcarp doctor` reports them

tests.name: Which GPUs JETCARP runs on
tests.about: one short run on each graphics adapter the doctor lists: which ones JETCARP uses, through which API, and why it leaves any out

tests.name: Anything that would skew the numbers?
tests.about: other JETCARP programs running, how busy the processor is, and whether a laptop is on battery: close what you can for numbers that compare

tests.name: JETCARP Hardware Score
tests.about: about a minute of JETCARP's own work, each answer checked; it names anything busy and asks first, and keeps nothing (`--no-save`)

tests.name: Parity: 16 scenes
tests.about: 16 scenes across the rule families and tilings, 300 generations each, on the processor and on the GPU JETCARP picks: every hash must match

tests.name: Parity: all 371 scenes on each GPU
tests.about: every scene, 300 generations, on the processor and on each GPU: every hash must match

tests.name: Parity: 40 scenes for 5,000 generations
tests.about: 40 scenes across every family and kind of tiling, 5,000 generations each, so that slow drift shows

tests.name: Parity on every other graphics API
tests.about: the 98 scenes on each adapter the earlier tests left out: the same GPU through another API (DirectX 12, OpenGL), and software renderers. One JETCARP won't use falls back to the processor, and says why

tests.name: Soup hunt with known results: Life
tests.about: 5,000 Life soups on squares from seed 1, on the processor and on each GPU: every count must be the known one

tests.name: Soup hunt with known results: hexagons
tests.about: 3,000 soups of B2/S34H on hexagons from seed 7, on the processor and on each GPU

tests.name: HashLife: a billion generations
tests.about: the Life scene jumped 2^30 generations on the unbounded plane: its population must be the known one

tests.name: Fit to this computer, off screen
tests.about: the desktop background's fit (`jetcarp host tune`) for a 1920 by 1080 screen, with no background host running, so it measures off screen; it shows nothing and saves nothing (`--dry-run`)

tests.name: Stepping speed
tests.about: generations a second of Life and of JACA on a 1024 by 1024 grid, on the processor and on each GPU; each must reach the same hash on all of them

tests.name: A 15-minute search, its memory watched
tests.about: an explore search over every tiling and rule family for 15 minutes, on every core but two and the GPU, its memory read every 5 seconds; it stops itself if it passes a quarter of this computer's memory
